g.text: NIGHTLY targets -- graded on a per-submission rerun
Phase 1: on submission -- mark the work, grade nothing
grading_mode is NIGHTLY, so the AI phase
grades nothing and spends no tokens here.
Tasks marked ai_needed stay NEEDED, so
what puts this submission in tonight's queue.
Phase 2: nightly -- trigger a rerun per submission
filter on grading_mode. Any submission with a
task still NEEDED qualifies, including one from
an IMMEDIATE assignment whose grading failed.
That failure self-heals overnight and the
student gets feedback next morning instead of
would leave such a task stuck forever, the
Rerun is per submission, so the trigger only
Still the one fragile step: Gradescope has no
public API, so locating a submission and
clicking its rerun button is UI automation and
will break when they reskin. Keep every
Consider throttling the loop. A term's worth
of submissions clicked as fast as Playwright
manages looks like abuse from the outside.
Phase 3: the rerun -- grade the NIGHTLY tasks
reasons other than our nightly job: an
instructor debugging the autograder, a TA
re-running a flaky test. None should re-bill
Same defensive write as in 03. Written before
grading, overwritten after. A container killed
mid-grading leaves the student with their test
results rather than a bare autograder error.
